daily.summary: Mandiant says a suspected China-nexus group exploited a VMware vCenter zero-day for two months before Broadcom's November 19 patch, and CISA has now listed it and three other flaws as exploited. Bell Canada, the European Commission and Amazon all describe intrusions using AI-driven tooling, including a China-linked operator whose agents found a zero-day. The FBI is reportedly investigating a breach of its national crime database, and West Virginia's legislature is responding to a cyberattack. Equinor says the attack on its IT systems has been stopped, with production unaffected.

weekly.summary: AI-assisted intrusion is the week's main theme: the FBI, Google, Unit 42 and Amazon describe autonomous attack frameworks in real operations, and Bell Canada and the European Commission say AI-driven attackers breached them. State-linked activity includes a China-nexus group's vCenter zero-day campaign, Russian espionage against Romanian government email and US organizations, and North Korean financial theft. Equinor's IT incident, now stopped with production unaffected, remains the most notable incident at an allied energy operator. Exploited flaws in vCenter, Cisco Expressway, Puppet, REDCap and refrigeration controllers, plus critical F5 BIG-IP and NGINX fixes, keep patching pressure high.
